relations.subject: tool:cblogredaction
relations.evidence: A tool to redact log files outside of Couchbase Server such as, SDK and cbbackupmgr log files.

notable_absence.finding: cblogredaction is a standalone, offline binary with no --cluster/--username/--password flags at all, no CB_REST_USERNAME/CB_REST_PASSWORD environment variables, and no CERTIFICATE AUTHENTICATION section - unlike every other page in this batch, which shares that entire authentication apparatus verbatim. This is the one page in the batch with NO authorization model whatsoever, RBAC or otherwise: it operates purely on local files the invoking OS user already has filesystem access to. Worth noting precisely because its total absence of the shared boilerplate confirms that boilerplate is templated per-subcommand rather than applied blindly - this genuinely different tool was correctly excluded from it.

cross_component_finding: Structurally this page is the odd one out in the batch: it has no SEE ALSO section and no 'Part of the couchbase-cli suite' footer, confirming DESCRIPTION's own claim that it is 'a tool to redact log files outside of Couchbase Server' - a genuinely separate binary shipped alongside couchbase-cli rather than one of its subcommands. Its own filename convention also breaks from the couchbase-cli-<subcommand> pattern used by all 12 other pages in this batch (no 'couchbase-cli-' prefix), consistent with it being packaged and documented independently.
cross_product_finding: The DESCRIPTION explicitly frames this tool's purpose across product boundaries: it redacts 'SDK and cbbackupmgr log files' - i.e. logs from Couchbase's SDK product family and from a separate Server CLI tool, not just couchbase-cli's own output. This is a rare instance in the batch of a page explicitly naming a cross-tool, cross-product scope for itself rather than being scoped to one component.
